lessons.title: Week 4 · Day 1 · Diagnose expressions and equations
lessons.body:
Unit 1 cumulative review · Diagnose expressions and equations
Objective: Distinguish expression simplification from equation solving, and justify each equality-preserving move.
Prerequisites: Weeks 1–3 algebraic equivalence, units, inequalities and real-world constraints.
Retrieval and diagnosis (5 min)
Individually predict the method before solving: Simplify 4(3a−2)−5a. Explain why this is the correct method.

Concept and worked example (12 min)
Simplify 3(2x−4)+5x: distribute to 6x−12+5x, then combine like terms to 11x−12. This is an equivalent expression, not an equation to solve. By contrast 3(2x−4)+5x=32 becomes 11x−12=32, 11x=44, x=4. Substitution: 3(8−4)+20=32. Learning target: Distinguish expression simplification from equation solving, and justify each equality-preserving move.

Guided evidence (12 min)
1. Simplify 4(3a−2)−5a. Compare methods with a partner, then justify each transformation.
2. Solve 4(3a−2)−5a=27. Compare methods with a partner, then justify each transformation.

Independent practice (16 min)
1. Simplify 2(4y+3)−3y. Include each algebraic step and a validity check.
2. Solve 2(4y+3)−3y=31. Include each algebraic step and a validity check.
3. Explain why 5y+6 is not a solution. Include each algebraic step and a validity check.

Individual check (5 min)
Solve 3(2z+1)−z=23 and check. Submit a reasoned response without consulting the teacher key.

Feedback and homework (5 min)
For homework, invent a new numeric instance of today's central mathematical structure and solve it in two ways or check by substitution. Identify a mistake to avoid: Distinguish expression simplification from equation solving, and justify each equality-preserving move. Use a large-print or spoken explanation if needed.
Accessibility and differentiation: provide high-contrast equations, chunked transformations, a two-column step/reason organizer, oral reasoning with transcription, extra processing time per approved plan, and optional challenge proofs. Keep independent checkpoint work independent.
learningTargets: Distinguish expression simplification from equation solving, and justify each equality-preserving move.

lessons.title: Week 4 · Day 2 · Classify equation solution sets
lessons.body:
Unit 1 cumulative review · Classify equation solution sets
Objective: Classify one-solution, identity and contradiction equations with explicit reasoning.
Prerequisites: Weeks 1–3 algebraic equivalence, units, inequalities and real-world constraints.
Retrieval and diagnosis (5 min)
Individually predict the method before solving: Classify 5(t+2)=5t+10. Explain why this is the correct method.

Concept and worked example (12 min)
For 2(3x+4)=6x+8, distribution gives 6x+8=6x+8, true for every real x. For 2(3x+4)=6x+9, subtraction yields 8=9, impossible; no solution. For 2(3x+4)=5x+8, simplify to x=0, one solution. Learning target: Classify one-solution, identity and contradiction equations with explicit reasoning.

Guided evidence (12 min)
1. Classify 5(t+2)=5t+10. Compare methods with a partner, then justify each transformation.
2. Classify 4(y+1)=4y+7. Compare methods with a partner, then justify each transformation.

Independent practice (16 min)
1. Classify 3(2m−1)=6m−3. Include each algebraic step and a validity check.
2. Classify 2(n+4)=2n+5. Include each algebraic step and a validity check.
3. Solve 7p+2=4p+17. Include each algebraic step and a validity check.

Individual check (5 min)
Classify 6(q−2)=6q−12 and justify. Submit a reasoned response without consulting the teacher key.

Feedback and homework (5 min)
For homework, invent a new numeric instance of today's central mathematical structure and solve it in two ways or check by substitution. Identify a mistake to avoid: Classify one-solution, identity and contradiction equations with explicit reasoning. Use a large-print or spoken explanation if needed.
Accessibility and differentiation: provide high-contrast equations, chunked transformations, a two-column step/reason organizer, oral reasoning with transcription, extra processing time per approved plan, and optional challenge proofs. Keep independent checkpoint work independent.

lessons.title: Week 4 · Day 3 · Reassess inequality reasoning
lessons.body:
Unit 1 cumulative review · Reassess inequality reasoning
Objective: Solve signed inequalities, interpret boundary inclusion, and test sample values.
Prerequisites: Weeks 1–3 algebraic equivalence, units, inequalities and real-world constraints.
Retrieval and diagnosis (5 min)
Individually predict the method before solving: Solve −2t+5<13. Explain why this is the correct method.

Concept and worked example (12 min)
Solve −3x+7≥19. Subtract 7: −3x≥12. Divide by negative 3 and reverse inequality: x≤−4. The boundary x=−4 gives 19≥19, included. x=0 gives 7≥19, false. Learning target: Solve signed inequalities, interpret boundary inclusion, and test sample values.

Guided evidence (12 min)
1. Solve −2t+5<13. Compare methods with a partner, then justify each transformation.
2. Solve 5−4n≤−7. Compare methods with a partner, then justify each transformation.

Independent practice (16 min)
1. Solve −5y−2>18. Include each algebraic step and a validity check.
2. Solve 2−3a≥−10. Include each algebraic step and a validity check.
3. Explain why the inequality reverses after dividing by −3. Include each algebraic step and a validity check.

Individual check (5 min)
Solve −4r+6≤22 and test r=−4. Submit a reasoned response without consulting the teacher key.

Feedback and homework (5 min)
For homework, invent a new numeric instance of today's central mathematical structure and solve it in two ways or check by substitution. Identify a mistake to avoid: Solve signed inequalities, interpret boundary inclusion, and test sample values. Use a large-print or spoken explanation if needed.
Accessibility and differentiation: provide high-contrast equations, chunked transformations, a two-column step/reason organizer, oral reasoning with transcription, extra processing time per approved plan, and optional challenge proofs. Keep independent checkpoint work independent.

lessons.title: Week 4 · Day 4 · Unit 1 transfer assessment
lessons.body:
Unit 1 cumulative review · Unit 1 transfer assessment
Objective: Independently combine expression structure, equation solving, inequalities and contextual interpretation.
Prerequisites: Weeks 1–3 algebraic equivalence, units, inequalities and real-world constraints.
Retrieval and diagnosis (5 min)
Individually predict the method before solving: Review: solve 5(x−2)=2x+8. Explain why this is the correct method.

Concept and worked example (12 min)
Before an assessment, model a separate example: A $12 fixed fee and $4 per item must stay within $44. Write 12+4n≤44, obtain n≤8, and verify 8 items cost $44. The independent assessment uses different values and is scored with a separate teacher-only key. Learning target: Independently combine expression structure, equation solving, inequalities and contextual interpretation.

Guided evidence (12 min)
1. Review: solve 5(x−2)=2x+8. Compare methods with a partner, then justify each transformation.
2. Review: solve −2a+1≤9. Compare methods with a partner, then justify each transformation.

Independent practice (16 min)
1. Checkpoint A: simplify 4(2x−3)+x. Include each algebraic step and a validity check.
2. Checkpoint B: solve 3(2x−1)=4x+9. Include each algebraic step and a validity check.
3. Checkpoint C: solve −3t+4≥16. Include each algebraic step and a validity check.
4. Checkpoint D: A club has $100 for a $16 fee plus $7 per participant. Find the maximum participants. Include each algebraic step and a validity check.

Individual check (5 min)
Identify the assessment problem you need to revisit and name the reasoning step to check. Submit a reasoned response without consulting the teacher key.

Feedback and homework (5 min)
For homework, invent a new numeric instance of today's central mathematical structure and solve it in two ways or check by substitution. Identify a mistake to avoid: Independently combine expression structure, equation solving, inequalities and contextual interpretation. Use a large-print or spoken explanation if needed.
Accessibility and differentiation: provide high-contrast equations, chunked transformations, a two-column step/reason organizer, oral reasoning with transcription, extra processing time per approved plan, and optional challenge proofs. Keep independent checkpoint work independent.

lessons.title: Week 4 · Day 5 · Targeted corrections and reassessment
lessons.body:
Unit 1 cumulative review · Targeted corrections and reassessment
Objective: Use assessment evidence to revise an error, demonstrate a new equivalent solution, and plan the next unit.
Prerequisites: Weeks 1–3 algebraic equivalence, units, inequalities and real-world constraints.
Retrieval and diagnosis (5 min)
Individually predict the method before solving: Correct: 3(x−2)=3x+2 implies x=8. Explain why this is the correct method.

Concept and worked example (12 min)
A student solves −2x≤8 as x≤−4. Test x=0: 0≤8 is true, yet 0≤−4 is false. The sign must reverse: x≥−4. An effective correction explains the negative division and verifies a boundary and interior value. Learning target: Use assessment evidence to revise an error, demonstrate a new equivalent solution, and plan the next unit.

Guided evidence (12 min)
1. Correct: 3(x−2)=3x+2 implies x=8. Compare methods with a partner, then justify each transformation.
2. Correct: $20 fixed + $5 each, $62 budget allows 9 items. Compare methods with a partner, then justify each transformation.

Independent practice (16 min)
1. Reassessment A: simplify 5(2a−1)−3a. Include each algebraic step and a validity check.
2. Reassessment B: solve 2(3x+1)=5x+9. Include each algebraic step and a validity check.
3. Reassessment C: solve −2m+3<11. Include each algebraic step and a validity check.
4. Reassessment D: At least 38 riders, 9 seats per vehicle. Minimum vehicles? Include each algebraic step and a validity check.

Individual check (5 min)
Write one original error you corrected and one substitution or boundary check proving your new answer. Submit a reasoned response without consulting the teacher key.

Feedback and homework (5 min)
For homework, invent a new numeric instance of today's central mathematical structure and solve it in two ways or check by substitution. Identify a mistake to avoid: Use assessment evidence to revise an error, demonstrate a new equivalent solution, and plan the next unit. Use a large-print or spoken explanation if needed.
Accessibility and differentiation: provide high-contrast equations, chunked transformations, a two-column step/reason organizer, oral reasoning with transcription, extra processing time per approved plan, and optional challenge proofs. Keep independent checkpoint work independent.
